verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents an official MCP server, both self-run and hosted, plus an official CLI (ldcli), API access tokens and flag creation, which gives an agent several documented paths to create and toggle flags. It also documents Approvals, role assignment and change history, which together let the platform route changes through review instead of writing straight to production. The evidence consists only of doc titles, though, and no item explicitly shows approvals being enforced on changes made through the API, CLI or MCP. Missing for 10: explicit evidence that approval workflows gate API/MCP/CLI-originated production changes, and independent or hands-on corroboration of agent-driven flag changes under approvals.
